concepts.def: Reactants are used up; products are formed in a reaction.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Chemical Reactions — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Chemical Reactions brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Chemical Reactions.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Blue hydrated copper(II) sulfate turns white on heating. Adding water to the white solid:
options: Turns it blue again, showing the change is reversible
Has no effect on it
Turns it black permanently
Releases chlorine gas

mcqs.q: Which change slows a reaction down?
options: Lowering the temperature
Adding a catalyst
Increasing the concentration
Grinding the solid more finely

mcqs.q: A graph of gas volume against time becomes horizontal when:
options: The reaction has finished
The catalyst has been used up
The gas has turned into a liquid
The temperature has reached zero

mcqs.q: In Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, the zinc is:
options: Oxidised
Reduced
Neutralised
Unchanged

mcqs.q: Does a catalyst increase the amount of product formed?
options: Catalysts slow reactions down to make them safer.
No — it only makes the product form faster; the final amount of product is unchanged.
The sulfate ions are reduced to sulfur.
Using a catalyst gives a higher yield as well as a faster reaction.
Melting is a chemical change because the solid turns into something that looks different.
Catalysts slow reactions down to make them safer.
No — melting is a physical change; no new substance is formed and the change is easily reversed by cooling.
Melting is a reaction because it needs energy to happen.

mcqs.q: In Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, which species is reduced?
options: Melting is a reaction because it needs energy to happen.
The Cu²⁺ ions are reduced — they gain electrons to form copper metal, while the zinc is oxidised.
The sulfate ions are reduced to sulfur.
The zinc is reduced because it disappears as it dissolves into the solution.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Rate of reaction”?
options: How quickly reactants are used up or products form, measured for example as volume of gas produced per unit time.
Oxidation is the loss of electrons and reduction is the gain of electrons; both always occur together in redox reactions.
Increasing concentration, temperature or surface area, or adding a catalyst, increases successful collisions and speeds up reactions.
A substance that increases the rate of a reaction without being used up, by lowering the activation energy.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Catalyst”?
options: A change that produces one or more new substances, usually with an energy transfer, and is not easily reversed.
A reaction that can go both ways, shown by the ⇌ symbol; hydrated copper(II) sulfate losing and regaining water is an example.
A substance that increases the rate of a reaction without being used up, by lowering the activation energy.
Increasing concentration, temperature or surface area, or adding a catalyst, increases successful collisions and speeds up reactions.
